sources.fullCitation: “United States-Mexico border crossing, Calexico, [1927?].” Los Angeles Times Photographic Collection, Library Special Collections, Charles E. Young Research Library, University of California, Los Angeles. Black-and-white nitrate negative, local identifier uclamss_1429_0385, ark:/21198/zz002d9ndg.
sources.researchNote: Calisphere presents the date as “[1927?]” in metadata supplied by UCLA; the year is not confirmed. The bird’s-eye view shows two security booths, cars and pedestrians, an arcaded building on the Mexican side and a sign arching over the road reading “Mexico”, with further signs for Mexicali, Southern Club Cafe, Cafe Gabrinus and Climax Cafe. The negative sleeve is annotated “Mexican American Line, Calexico, Mexicali” and “California, Calexico-Mexicali”. The catalogue suggests a possible connection to two Los Angeles Times reports from Calexico, “No Permit Needed at Mexican Border” of 6 July 1927 and “New Regulations in Force at Border” of 14 July 1927, but does not confirm publication.
sources.title: United States-Mexico border crossing, Calexico, [1927?]
sources.creator: Los Angeles Times (photographer unidentified)
sources.repository: UCLA Library Special Collections, Charles E. Young Research Library

sources.shortCitation: UCLA, Walter Jurmann Collection (APAM-1), Box 1, Folder 6 — Melodie der Liebe song folio
sources.fullCitation: Finding Aid for the Walter Jurmann Collection, 1910–1988, Collection APAM-1. UCLA Library, Performing Arts Special Collections, Los Angeles; processed by Juliane Brand, 1989. Box 1, Folder 6: Melodie der Liebe: ein Reichsliga-Film der Heros / Worte von Fritz Rotter; Musik von Dr. B. Kaper und Walter Jurmann. Berlin: Alrobi Musikverlag, [1932]; photocopy of cover only. Contents: Ein Lied aus meiner Heimat; Schade, daß Liebe ein Märchen ist!; Wie gern möcht’ ich Dich verwöhnen!; Kinderlied (Es war einmal ein Baby). Online Archive of California, ark:/13030/kt5779q3vh.
sources.title: Walter Jurmann Collection — Melodie der Liebe song folio
sources.repository: UCLA Library, Performing Arts Special Collections
sources.researchNote: The earlier APAM-1 finding aid lists the four songs of the Melodie der Liebe folio and gives the fourth as “Kinderlied (Es war einmal ein Baby--)”; its title index cross-refers that title to Melodie der Liebe. The public link opens the current UCLA finding aid, Collection 2271, which lists the cover reproduction in Box 1, Folder 6 but does not list the four song titles in that entry. Neither finding aid reproduces the score.

sources.shortCitation: Finding Aid, Walter Jurmann Collection — scope note on “The Magic of Springtime”
sources.fullCitation: Finding Aid for the Walter Jurmann Collection, 1910–1988, Collection APAM-1. UCLA Library, Performing Arts Special Collections, Los Angeles; processed by Juliane Brand, 1989. Scope and Content note: the Papers of Gus Kahn in the Archive of Popular American Music include “an ozalid copy of a presumably unpublished Jurmann/Kaper/Kahn song, ‘The Magic of Springtime’, originally written for but never used in the 1936 MGM film ‘Maytime’”.
sources.title: Walter Jurmann Collection finding aid — The Magic of Springtime in the Gus Kahn Papers
sources.creator: Juliane Brand
sources.repository: UCLA Library, Performing Arts Special Collections
sources.researchNote: The cited passage was checked in a copy of the earlier APAM-1 finding aid. The current online finding aid for the Gus Kahn Papers describes film music for Maytime but does not identify this song by title; it is linked as collection context, not as the source of the quoted passage. The earlier finding aid describes Maytime as a 1936 film. The AFI Catalog dates its release to 26 March 1937 and records production in 1936–1937; the earlier wording is retained in the citation.
